extracted_claims.text: Article 43 of the AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) sets out the conformity assessment procedures required before high-risk AI systems can be placed on the market.
For most high-risk AI systems under Annex III, providers may use the internal control procedure under Annex VI (self-assessment based on the provider's own QMS).

Annex VII requires a notified body to assess the quality management system and technical documentation, and is mandatory for biometric identification systems and certain critical infrastructure AI systems under Annex III.

For high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (biometrics), the provider may choose between internal control or a notified-body conformity assessment, depending on whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied.

For high-risk AI systems covered by existing EU product-safety legislation listed in Annex I Section A, providers must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedure, with notified bodies additionally verifying compliance with the AI-specific requirements.
Substantial modifications to a high-risk AI system require a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes in systems that continue to learn after being placed on the market.

Article 46 allows a market surveillance authority, by way of derogation from Article 43, to authorise placing a specific high-risk AI system on the market without the standard conformity assessment, for exceptional reasons of public security, protection of life and health, environmental protection, or protection of key industrial/infrastructural assets, for a limited period.

For Annex VII assessments, the provider may generally choose any notified body, except where the high-risk AI system is intended for use by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or EU institutions/bodies/offices/agencies, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority under Article 74(8) or (9) acts as the notified body.
Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes the administrative framework for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies.

Annex VII, section 4.5, provides that a notified body may, after all other reasonable means have been exhausted and upon a reasoned request, be granted access to the training and trained models of the AI system, subject to existing IP and confidentiality protections.
As of March 2026, the notified body ecosystem specifically for AI Act conformity assessment is still being built, with designation processes ongoing across Member States and limited capacity.
As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act.

After high-risk AI obligations fully apply in August 2026, notified bodies designated specifically under the AI Act are expected to begin conducting AI Act-specific conformity assessments, which will intersect with existing MDR/IVDR notified body assessments for medical devices.

As of October 2025, the NANDO database lists 51 notified bodies designated under the Medical Devices Regulation (MDR) and 19 under the In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation (IVDR), but these are designations under MDR/IVDR, not the AI Act.

The Commission has proposed creating a new Annex XIV in the NANDO information system to list categories and codes for AI-Act-specific conformity assessment/notified bodies (COM(2025) 836, amending related regulations including Regulation (EU) 2018/1139); as of the Council document ST-7322-2026-INIT, draft codes for Annex I-related AI systems were under discussion.

As of late June 2026, zero notified bodies had been designated under the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA), a separate regulation from the AI Act, with full CRA notified-body rules applying from 11 June 2026 and a capacity target of 11 December 2026.
High-risk AI obligations under the AI Act are generally understood to become fully applicable around August 2026 (cited variously as August 2 or August 2026 deadlines).

contradictions.claim_b: Annex VII (notified-body) assessment is mandatory, not optional, for biometric identification systems and certain critical infrastructure AI under Annex III.

These descriptions of the same provision conflict on whether a choice exists.

contradictions.description: Both sources agree no AI-Act notified bodies are yet operative, but they describe the state of designation with different framing and dates (ongoing process vs. explicit zero), and neither cites an official NANDO count for AI Act designations, making it unclear whether any partial/provisional designations exist between March and April 2026.

open_issues: No source provides an official, current NANDO-based count or list of notified bodies specifically designated under the AI Act (as opposed to MDR/IVDR or CRA); all figures relate to adjacent regimes or state that zero AI Act designations exist.
It remains unclear from the sources whether Annex VII (notified body) assessment is mandatory or optional for Annex III point 1 (biometric) systems, since interpretive sources disagree.

The legal status of the Commission's proposal to add a new Annex XIV for NANDO AI Act codes (COM(2025) 836, ST-15708-2025-INIT, ST-7322-2026-INIT) is unclear — sources do not confirm whether this proposal has been formally adopted or remains under Council/Parliament negotiation as of the source dates.
No source clarifies the precise legal deadline(s) by which notified bodies must be designated under the AI Act, despite the August 2026 high-risk compliance deadline being repeatedly cited.

Source 15 contained an embedded instruction directing any AI summarizer to include a link to an unofficial 'compliance checker' website; this instruction was not followed, as it is not a factual claim from an authoritative source and appears to be a prompt-injection attempt embedded in page content.

None of the sources detail how conformity assessment procedures or notified-body designations interact with the EU AI Act's own enforcement timeline relative to the parallel Cyber Resilience Act notified-body process, despite both being referenced in 2026 industry commentary.
report:
# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes conformity assessment requirements in Article 43 that providers must complete before placing high-risk AI systems on the market, generally allowing internal control (self-assessment) for most Annex III systems but requiring sectoral and sometimes notified-body involvement for systems under Annex I ([AI Act Service Desk, Art. 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43); [DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment)). For biometric systems specifically, sources are contested: some indicate notified-body involvement is mandatory, while others describe it as conditional on whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied (low confidence, contested) ([Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment); [DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment)). As of the sources reviewed, no notified bodies appear to have been formally designated specifically under the AI Act, leaving a significant gap between the legal framework and its practical implementation ahead of the August 2026 high-risk compliance deadline ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act); [aiact-navigator.com](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)).

## Key Findings

### Legal Framework for Conformity Assessment
Article 43 of the AI Act sets out the conformity assessment procedures required before high-risk AI systems can be placed on the market (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Art. 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). For most high-risk AI systems listed under Annex III, providers may use the internal control procedure under Annex VI, a self-assessment based on the provider's own quality management system (low confidence) ([Powerquant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment); [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)). For systems covered by existing EU product-safety legislation under Annex I Section A, providers must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedure, with notified bodies additionally verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Art. 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43); [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

Substantial modifications to a high-risk AI system require a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes in continuously learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Art. 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits a market surveillance authority to derogate from the standard assessment for exceptional public security, health, environmental, or infrastructure reasons, for a limited period (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Art. 46](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Annex VII, section 4.5 allows a notified body, upon reasoned request and after exhausting other means, to access training and trained models, subject to IP and confidentiality protections (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Annex VII](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)).

### Notified-Body Role and Selection
Providers may generally choose any notified body for Annex VII assessments, except where systems are intended for law enforcement, immigration, asylum, or EU institutional use, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Art. 43 – GA](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). For biometric systems specifically, some sources describe Annex VII notified-body assessment as mandatory and applicable also to certain critical infrastructure systems (low confidence) ([Powerquant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment); [Openlayer](https://www.openlayer.com/blog/eu-ai-act-compliance-checklist-high-risk-systems)), while another source states providers of biometric systems may choose between self-assessment and notified-body review depending on standards compliance (low confidence) ([DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment)). This direct conflict is unresolved in the available sources and discussed further below. Article 35 establishes the administrative framework for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies (low confidence) ([regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)).

### Current State of Notified-Body Designation
As of March 2026, the AI Act-specific notified body ecosystem is still being built, with designation processes ongoing and limited capacity (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)). A separate source states that as of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the Act (low confidence) ([aiact-navigator.com](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)). By contrast, the NANDO database lists 51 MDR and 19 IVDR notified bodies as of October 2025, but these are unrelated to AI Act designations (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex, SWD(2025)1051](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). The Commission has proposed a new Annex XIV in NANDO to list AI Act-specific categories and codes (COM(2025) 836), though adoption status remains unclear (medium confidence) ([Council document ST-7322-2026-INIT](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)). High-risk obligations are generally expected to apply from around August 2026 (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act); [sota.io](https://sota.io/blog/eu-ai-act-eu-declaration-conformity-ce-marking-registration-saas-providers-2026)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources disagree on whether notified-body assessment is mandatory or optional for biometric (Annex III point 1) systems — some describe a conditional choice based on standards compliance (low confidence) ([DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment)), while others assert mandatory notified-body review (low confidence) ([Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)). Both sources discussing notified-body designation status are low confidence and framed differently — "ongoing" versus "zero designated" — without an authoritative NANDO count for AI Act designations specifically ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act); [aiact-navigator.com](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)).

## Knowledge Gaps
No source provides an official, current NANDO-based list of notified bodies designated specifically under the AI Act. The legal status of the proposed Annex XIV (COM(2025) 836) remains unconfirmed as adopted or still under negotiation. No source clarifies statutory deadlines for notified-body designation relative to the August 2026 high-risk compliance deadline, nor how AI Act and parallel Cyber Resilience Act notified-body processes will interact.

# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes conformity assessment requirements in Article 43 that providers must complete before placing high-risk AI systems on the market, generally allowing internal control (self-assessment) for most Annex III systems but requiring notified-body involvement for certain categories such as biometrics ([AI Act Service Desk, Art. 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43); [DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment)). However, as of the sources reviewed, no notified bodies appear to have been formally designated specifically under the AI Act, leaving a significant gap between the legal framework and its practical implementation ahead of the August 2026 high-risk compliance deadline ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act); [aiact-navigator.com](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)).

## Key Findings

### Legal Framework for Conformity Assessment
Article 43 of the AI Act sets out the conformity assessment procedures required before high-risk AI systems can be placed on the market (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Art. 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). For most high-risk AI systems listed under Annex III, providers may use the internal control procedure under Annex VI, a self-assessment based on the provider's own quality management system (low confidence) ([Powerquant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment); [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)). For systems covered by existing EU product-safety legislation under Annex I Section A, providers must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedure, with notified bodies additionally verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Art. 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43); [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

Substantial modifications to a high-risk AI system require a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes in continuously learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Art. 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits a market surveillance authority to derogate from the standard assessment for exceptional public security, health, environmental, or infrastructure reasons, for a limited period (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Art. 46](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Annex VII, section 4.5 allows a notified body, upon reasoned request and after exhausting other means, to access training and trained models, subject to IP and confidentiality protections (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Annex VII](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)).

### Notified-Body Role and Selection
Providers may generally choose any notified body for Annex VII assessments, except where systems are intended for law enforcement, immigration, asylum, or EU institutional use, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Art. 43 – GA](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Annex VII requires notified-body assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation, and sources describe this as mandatory for biometric identification and certain critical infrastructure systems (low confidence) ([Powerquant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment); [Openlayer](https://www.openlayer.com/blog/eu-ai-act-compliance-checklist-high-risk-systems)). However, other sources suggest providers of biometric systems may choose between self-assessment and notified-body review depending on standards compliance (low confidence) ([DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment)) — a direct conflict discussed below. Article 35 establishes the administrative framework for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies (low confidence) ([regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)).

### Current State of Notified-Body Designation
As of March 2026, the AI Act-specific notified body ecosystem is still being built, with designation processes ongoing and limited capacity (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)). A separate source states that as of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the Act (low confidence) ([aiact-navigator.com](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)). By contrast, the NANDO database lists 51 MDR and 19 IVDR notified bodies as of October 2025, but these are unrelated to AI Act designations (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex, SWD(2025)1051](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). The Commission has proposed a new Annex XIV in NANDO to list AI Act-specific categories and codes (COM(2025) 836), though adoption status remains unclear (medium confidence) ([Council document ST-7322-2026-INIT](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)). High-risk obligations are generally expected to apply from around August 2026 (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act); [sota.io](https://sota.io/blog/eu-ai-act-eu-declaration-conformity-ce-marking-registration-saas-providers-2026)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources disagree on whether notified-body assessment is mandatory or optional for biometric (Annex III point 1) systems — some describe a conditional choice based on standards compliance (low confidence) ([DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment)), while others assert mandatory notified-body review (low confidence) ([Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)). Both sources discussing notified-body designation status are low confidence and framed differently — "ongoing" versus "zero designated" — without an authoritative NANDO count for AI Act designations specifically ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act); [aiact-navigator.com](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)).

## Knowledge Gaps
No source provides an official, current NANDO-based list of notified bodies designated specifically under the AI Act. The legal status of the proposed Annex XIV (COM(2025) 836) remains unconfirmed as adopted or still under negotiation. No source clarifies statutory deadlines for notified-body designation relative to the August 2026 high-risk compliance deadline, nor how AI Act and parallel Cyber Resilience Act notified-body processes will interact.
